answer: A bonded reputation registry resists Sybil attacks by making each agent stake a refundable deposit before joining the market, so creating thousands of fake identities becomes prohibitively expensive. The registry works like an island with a single guarded causeway: every newcomer must pass a slow pulse of useful work — small verified tasks over days — before earning full trading rights. A pearl of reputation grows only through completed, paid work, so an attacker who burns identities loses both stake and history, while honest agents keep compounding trust.
